items.title: Joel Dorn interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 13, 2007
items.q: So I signed her... we made the record... we had money for seven strings... we do the album

ctx.x: But I didn’t do it because I was smart, I did it because I said oh let me see if they’ll give me a royalty. You know, Mr. Simpson.

I was looking at that, I’m a type of person who just thinks it’s so neat when you see Bucky Pizzarelli here and all these musicians who can move from one genre to another, and a producer who can do that too. So when I looked on Robert Flack’s first record and then I see Bucky Pizzarelli and I say now how did he end up on that record? © Fillius Jazz Archive -9-

Simple. The arranger hired him. I never met Bucky. Let me tell you about that first record. Rahsaan had called me up from Washington and he said, “I’ve got a girl singer for you.” I said, “what’s her name?” He said, “Roberta Novosel, she’s married to my bass player, Steve Novosel.” I said okay. And I said to him, “what does she sound like?” And he got mad and he said, “she sounds like a colored lady” and he slammed the phone down, you know? I don’t know what I said, you know, what does she sound like? About a…
